chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and others, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Be either a knowledgeable one, a student, or a lover of the scholars, and do not be the fourth group, lest you perish due to your enmity of them.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people regarding knowledge and the fourth group that perishes?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal establishes a hierarchical spiritual status for the three groups engaged with knowledge, emphasizing that loving scholars is a virtuous act in itself, not merely a passive state. The warning against the fourth group highlights the Shia concept of 'ghibah' (occultation) and the importance of maintaining affection for the Ahl al-Bayt and their successors to avoid spiritual ruin. It underscores the communal responsibility to support the transmission of religious knowledge through both active learning and supportive love.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-117 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Safvan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Abi Ayoob al-Khizaz, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim and others, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“Be either a knowledgeable one, a student or a friend of the knowledgeable ones. Do not be of any other group since then you would be destroyed due to their enmity.”
